reviews.review: Great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Very reminiscent of the gear of wars series. Definitely a must try. Trust me. Main character is a badass.
Still holds up even after all these years, looking forward to the sequel!

Like many warhammer 40k games I've played - this is a mixed bag.

PROs: 
+ You live out the power trip of an UltraMarine. Swinging a big hammer and smashing down from a jetpack jump is where this game shines.
+ Lore. As typical in 40k games, the ambiance and lore (if you are into that thing) are compelling. Seeing the various factions and other aspects of the 40k universe in here are immersive.
+ Cutscenes. I enjoyed the story and the cutscenes. While standard fare , it satisfied my 40k universe hunger.

CONS
- Enemies Spongy AF. If you like feeling like a badass UltraMarine, but with a wet noodle and pea shooter for weapons. This is the game for you. Enemies take days to eliminate. It's kinda ludicrous.
- Rudimentary level design. Developed in 2011. Level design from 1991. Feels like OG Doom level design (that's an insult to Doom really)
- Janky, Awkward and Clunky are 3 words that very accurately describe the feel and gameplay.
- Length. Years ago I picked this game up, hated it, tried it again couple years later, still hated it, tried it again now, sort of liked it enough to finish it finally - and still only clocked in at 9 total hours. That's pretty short.

If the anniversary edition was introduced and set a price that was reflective of a game that is 12+ years old already (and looks/feels like it) and maybe 2/3rds of what it's listed as (currently SIXTY DOLLARS!!), then maybe that would have swayed me to an overall positive for the cost of nostalgia and the 40k universe. But at $60 dollars - that's laughable.  Nothing in GW is cheap, and neither is the base cost of this game. 


If you truly are a 40k universe fan, need to feel the power of an Ultra Marine and want some mindless fun - it's worth at a very deep discount due to it showing it's age in many areas. Otherwise, it's tough to give a thumbs up on the current price point for the value.
